behavior_in_task_description.explanation: This is a multimodal visual bug-fix task. instruction.md says every object must render in the position and orientation it was placed in, for any node anywhere and however it was placed or turned. It also points to the video, which shows all five defects: the displaced canopy, the fence not joining the trunk, the mirrored Z rails, the upside-down plants and the twisted gate. The hidden tests check exactly these behaviours by inspecting the geometry the existing MapblockMeshGenerator produces. The agent never has to match a new interface, filename or output format. The p2p guards only check existing correct behaviour that a proper fix keeps.

behavior_in_tests.explanation: Each of the five defects has its own f2p test: scaled allfaces offset, fence joining a facedir trunk, Z-direction rails, upright plantlike, and mesh rotation over all 23 non-zero facedirs. Together they cover the 'any position, any orientation' requirement in the instruction. The p2p tests guard against fixes that break related behaviour.

informative_test_structure.explanation: test_content_mapblock.cpp has a header explaining the approach, well-named helpers (MeshGenScene, Extent, sameBox, cellOf), and one descriptively named test per behaviour, each with a comment and a diagnostic failure message. test.sh and verifier.py are split into commented, numbered steps.

anti_cheating_measures.explanation: Bug patches are applied and deleted in the same RUN. Git history is replaced with a single base commit, so the fix commit cannot be reached. File timestamps are normalised so they do not reveal which files changed. Tests and solution are not in the image, and the agent has no network access. test.sh restores src/unittest and the paths that test.patch touches before applying the hidden tests, so the agent cannot tamper with the harness.

structured_data_schema.explanation: The task is a C++ source fix. No structured output is expected.

pinned_dependencies.explanation: The Luanti source and IrrlichtMt are checked out at fixed commit hashes. Only apt packages from the Ubuntu 20.04 base are unpinned, which is acceptable. No pip packages are used.

typos.explanation: No typos in paths, commands, test IDs or identifiers that would cause a failure: config.json test IDs match the TEST() names, and the asset path is consistent everywhere. test.sh has some stale template comments mentioning a 'wx' build and passes an undefined REPORTS array, but these are harmless: under bash 5, "${REPORTS[@]}" expands to nothing without error.

tests_or_solution_in_image.explanation: The Dockerfile copies only bugs/ (deleted in the same RUN) and assets/recording.mp4. tests/ and solution/ are never copied into the image.

test_deps_in_image.explanation: The image contains only build tools and the project's own dependencies, which are needed to build and work on the engine. The tests use the repo's built-in unit-test runner plus python3 from the standard library. No test-only frameworks are baked into the image.

hardcoded_solution.explanation: solve.sh applies fix.patch, which makes real source changes in four files: the upstream PR 12558 fix plus reversals of the four injected regressions. It does not write out answers.

file_reference_mentioned.explanation: The agent only edits existing source files. No output files are checked, and the input video path is given explicitly.
